Hi Samir — thanks for sending the matrix and flagging this.

Short answer: for Redwood to accept the exemption and release the invoice hold, the certificate must clearly list the legal selling entity that appears on the invoice (the "Remit To / Bill To" name). If your AP will pay under 'Acme Logistics, Inc.' the certificate should name that legal entity.

Two quick notes:
- If the certificate lists only the DBAs (e.g., 'Acme Logistics - West Region') we need an additional document tying the DBA to the legal entity (signed affidavit or a certificate of assumed name).
- We also need an expiration date on the certificate or an indication that it's a blanket certificate covering the period of the PO.

Can you have your tax team send a PDF of the signed certificate naming 'Acme Logistics, Inc.'? If they can instead provide a signed letter tying the DBA to the parent company, that's acceptable but will require a short internal review.

Cc'ing Markus from finance to confirm whether any additional fields are required on our invoice for your AP (tax ID masking, remit address).

Best,
Camila Reyes

Camila / Karthik — quick internal note before we respond to Acme:

1) If the certificate lists 'Acme Logistics, Inc.' we're good and can clear the hold once we verify the signer (name/title) matches the signatory block and the certificate scope applies to software/services.
2) If they provide a DBA-only certificate, we will need their affidavit tying DBA -> parent and a W-9 or substitute form that matches the billing entity. That will add ~2 business days for verification.
3) If the certificate is dated but lacks an explicit blanket indicator, request either a date range or a blanket statement.

I'll stand by to process the PDF when it comes through.
